utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could you call the number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Case Number IT-01-47-T, The Prosecutor versus Enver Hadzihasanovic and Amir Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Could we have the appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, good morning, Your Honours. Good morning counsel. For the Prosecution Daryl Mundis, Ekkehard Withopf, and the case manager Ruth Karper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Withopf. And the appearances for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours. On behalf of General Hadzihasanovic, Edina Residovic, counsel, and Stephane Bourgon co-counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Your Honours. On behalf of Mr. Kubura, Rodney Dixon, Fahrudin Ibrisimovic, and Mr. Mulalic our legal assistant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Trial Chamber would like to greet everyone present in the courtroom, the Prosecution, the Defence, the accused, and everyone else. As you are aware, at the request of the Prosecution, we will be working for longer hours today. The Registrar has informed me that we can start working again at 2.45 after the break, which will start at 1.45. We will have a one-hour break, and we will resume at 2.45. But we will only have an hour and a half, given the interpreters' obligations. I hope that this additional time will allow us to conclude the hearing of the witness who is here and start hearing the second witness. I'd like to remind the parties to ask questions that are essential because your questions are to inform the Tribunal about the facts, about what happened, so it is necessary to ask essential questions. Sometimes the questions put to a witness are not very useful. So this is an effort you should make. Questions should put which are useful for the Defence and for the Prosecution. If the Judges think that additional questions are needed, we will put them to the witness. But it is better if the parties put the questions, rather than the Judges. If the Judges ask questions, this will just be to fill in any shortcomings. Could the usher please call the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Witness. I hope you're receiving the interpretation. We will continue with your testimony today. And I believe that you'll be able to go back to your country today. In fact, we had already started the cross-examination, so the Defence may take the floor. I was thinking of the Prosecution's re-examination. But the Defence still has questions to put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Good day, Mr. Kiggell

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yesterday, before we broke, you spoke about a number of reasons, and you confirmed that these were possible reasons for which it was necessary for you to have permission from the 3rd Corps command to pass through checkpoints. This concerned the vicinity of the front line and the security of UNPROFOR. Do you remember us discussing this subject yesterday?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, apart from the situations we mentioned, you can certainly confirm that sometimes the soldiers at checkpoints expressed their dissatisfaction because of the permission you had been given, and they asked for authorisation and the agreement of their local commanders. Did you witness such events?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, quite often I would have to get permission from the local brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that was obviously proof that the BH army was having great difficulty when being formed, and sometimes the local commanders had actual power. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In fact, during your stay in Zenica, it was quite obvious that the BH army, in spite of all the efforts it made, was not able to establish its structure up to the line of subordination, which is usual for an army which is well organised. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were problems with communication, and this would delay our sort of trip through the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As a professional soldier, you are certainly aware of the fact that in conditions of peace, in order to form a corps, several years are required; whereas the 3rd Corps was being formed in conditions which are very unfavourable, two wars were being waged. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: During your stay in Zenica, you were aware of the fact that the 3rd Corps held the line towards the Serbian forces. It was several hundred kilometres long. It was exposed to constant attacks. And in 1993, another front was opened up, a front facing the HVO. Were you aware of this fact?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You may also have witnessed a situation in which the commander and deputy commander, in order to secure your position, they would sometimes negotiate with local commanders instead of issuing orders. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, as you said yesterday, the 3rd Corps commander was a professional officer. And it was difficult for him to admit in front of you that the system of command and control was still not functioning in the army. So he sought to justify his soldiers in various ways. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would say that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When my learned colleague from the Prosecution asked you what the purpose of your liaison officer was, you said that Mr. Hadzihasanovic complained to Lieutenant Colonel Duncan, that you were collating too much information, and in your opinion this could be something like a countermeasure taken by the 3rd Corps. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that seemed to be the case at the time. I was going round, getting a lot of information. And the 3rd Corps commander played the same game, assigned a liaison officer to me to, you know, replicate what we were doing.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, as a professional soldier and a soldier who was trained before arriving in Bosnia and Herzegovina, you were certainly aware of the difference between the UN mission in accordance with the Chapter 6 of the UN charter and the mission according to Chapter 7 of the UN charter. Were you aware of the difference between these two things?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't obviously recall what the difference between the two chapters were. I know what our UN mission was at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps in order to refresh your memory, I could say that Chapter 7 of the charter provide for establishing peace and enabled the UN forces to use force in order to establish peace; whereas the mission that you took part in pursuant to Chapter 6 of the charter was only a mission, the purpose of which was to support the delivery of humanitarian aid provided for in this UN chapter. You didn't have a mandate to establish peace; your mandate was to provide humanitarian aid. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. We were there to provide conditions where aid Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. could be delivered.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You're aware of the fact that that mission, providing support when delivering humanitarian aid, included firstly taking -- meant that the measures taken couldn't influence the rights of the parties involved in the conflict or the measures that they would take. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we were there to support the delivery of aid in the area. We weren't to intervene in the fighting.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You're also aware of the fact that the UN support was provided, with the agreement with all the parties concerned, and the agreement of the BH state. In this territory you were active. Were you aware of this fact?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Similarly, and this was your testimony yesterday, as soldiers, it was your responsibility to provide such support for humanitarian aid, but you were only allowed to use force when it was a matter of legitimate self-defense. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And even as far as using the right to defend yourselves, there were rules according to which force could only be used as a last resort. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. It's known as the rules of engagement.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So as you were very familiar with the nature of your mission, you knew that the BH army wasn't obliged to let the liaison officer, or rather, UNPROFOR members, move around freely in the vicinity of the combat lines. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our mission was to move freely in the area. And if I recall correctly, you know, we could get through checkpoints. Sometimes we would be delayed getting through them, perhaps because they didn't want UNPROFOR to go into the area because of what operations were going on. And it was said that as -- so for our own security as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. Although I can follow what you're saying, it would be more precise if I listened to the interpretation. Thank you. However, as far as you are aware, UNPROFOR attempted to avoid any sort of activity that could be interpreted as getting involved in the positions taken by the parties in the conflict. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your battalion, or the mission that was assigned to you, could not collate intelligence in the way that battalions engaged in a conflict do. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, your testimony before this Court was that it was your duty to collate information on the BH army, the positions of its units, their military officers, and the existing or future combat operations. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, you also stated that the reason for which you did this, in order to ensure -- was in order to ensure the security of humanitarian convoys and the British soldiers. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, just to get an accurate picture of what was going on in our area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, these broadly defined activities of yours could give rise to suspicion, and the army involved in the conflict might believe that you were going beyond the scope of your mandate. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very possibly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As the British army is part of NATO, you know that the idea of liaison officer within NATO is such that such an officer only establishes contact between two armies in a conflict. The armies, then, reach certain agreements and implement these agreements. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Withopf.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecution objects against this question. The witness was in the area of Central Bosnia under the auspices of UNPROFOR. And this question is related to customs used within NATO. This appears to go beyond the scope what can be asked in cross-examination. And it certainly wasn't an issue that has been addressed in examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this is just one of a number of questions I wanted to put to the witness in order to clarify an answer provided by the witness yesterday as to why a 3rd Corps commander would introduce or assign a liaison officer. But I don't think it's that important for the witness to answer this question, as he has provided sufficient explanation. So I will withdraw the question to avoid any further debate.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So, Witness, you could agree with me and you have already said that this is the case, the way you proceeded when carrying out your mission may have resulted in a corps commander assigning a liaison officer, and that would be in accordance with his position. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, you spoke about how you collated certain information. Would you agree with me if I told you that even such a manner of collating information, the manner used by the British Battalion, was, in fact, a reduced manner of collating information. It was a sort of restricted way of gathering information, the kind of information that a battalion involved in combat would usually gather. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because all we could do is either talk to the people concerned or have the people physically on the ground observing what occurred.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So what you would usually have done as a battalion involved in combat in order to obtain reliable information, for example, using certain means of gathering information, ways of checking information, these methods weren't accessible to you and these weren't methods that you used. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, in addition to the fact that your activities could be interpreted as going beyond the scope of the mandate, you nevertheless confirmed yesterday that the corps commander and the deputy commander and the liaison officer tried to make it possible for you to gain access to all the information you were interested in. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Similarly, in the building of the 3rd Corps command, you were given access to all sections of the command that you were interested in. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was assigned the liaison officer, so he was the point of contact to get information.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: According to your testimony yesterday, you were in Zenica for not even three and a half months before you went to Tuzla. From the 21st of May to the 31st of August?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also mentioned the daily meetings that you had in the battalion command. My question is: Would it be correct to say that quite frequently at those daily meetings which were held at 1800 hours in Vitez, many of your colleagues, officers from the BritBat who should have attended these meetings, didn't do so because they were involved in other operative tasks at the time?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was true. There were occasions when everybody was not available due to operations.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The milinfosum which were drafted contained all the relevant information presented by those who attended the meeting. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not exactly correct. The information was collated from everybody operating on the ground, which were then debriefed, the intelligence officer. He would then give a brief on that information gathered to the meeting at 1800. Then additionally, the officers present there would give a short summary of what they had been doing that day.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Reports which were compiled in this way were reports that you did Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. not forward to the parties involved in the conflict. Is that right? The milinfosum -- the milinfosums weren't sent to the 3rd Corps command. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, because it reported activities on all sides.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: BritBat's relationship to the parties in the conflict were relationships that you had at meetings or when there were official records concerning BritBat and the 3rd Corps command. Is that how you communicated with them?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, can you clarify your question, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, gladly. You said that you did not forward your information to the parties involved in the conflict; that is to say, to the 3rd Corps and the HVO. However, when you discussed certain issues, this was done either by having individual meetings between you and other officers, or you had contact at organised meetings attended by a number of individuals, or there was an official record which you would provide to the party concerned; in this case, the 3rd Corps. Is this how you communicated with the 3rd Corps, or on the other hand with the HVO on the other side?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was a series of meetings that we had. We had sent letters, telephone calls. It was just any level of communication we could have.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Similarly, the parties involved in the conflict, the 3rd Corps, too, did not provide BritBat with their military plans, their orders or reports on activities carried out unless they were directly related to an UNPROFOR request. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now like to move on to another area that you have discussed with the Prosecution. In response to a question put to you by the Prosecution, you said that you had the opportunity of meeting Mujahedin; that is to say, foreign combatants who were in the area of Central Bosnia while you were there. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At that time, you saw that some of the local Muslims joined these foreign combatants. Is that the information you had?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it would seem that the local Muslims joined the Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Similarly, on the basis of what you personally observed, you saw that some of the local inhabitants were imitating these foreigners, both as far as the clothes they wore are concerned or the beards they wore, or perhaps they adhered more strictly to religious principles. Were you in a position to observe such behaviour?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we saw that -- this -- of the local Muslims who were more fundamental in their Muslim faith developed, growing the beards and the clothing.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, a significant part of the local population was afraid of the Mujahedin and did not approve their behaviour and their presence there. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I have understood this correctly, when you explained the nature of your meetings with these foreign combatants, with the Mujahedin, you said that the first time you met them was in a cafe, and they were unarmed foreigners on that occasion. On the second occasion, you spoke to a group who said they were from Turkey, and the third time was in the village of Arnauti. Have I understood you correctly when you spoke about your meetings with these foreigners?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I may have met them on more than one occasion, but this one I can definitely recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness now be shown milinfosum dated the 30th of May 1993. This is necessary in order for me to be able to ask the witness a number of questions. I apologise. I meant the 31st of May 1993, and not the 30th of May.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please tell me whether in paragraph 3 of this milinfosum there is reference to your own information as a liaison officer in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. It refers to the Zenica LO, which was me at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On that day, you spoke with three Mujahedin who said that they were from Turkey. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: They didn't tell you anything about their military affiliation, nor about their relations with the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, did they?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You inferred that they were not under the control of the 3rd Corps. Is that what it says here?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would seem to be the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Will you please look at paragraph 4. This paragraph also relates to your contact in Zenica, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On that day, you met Jasmin Saric, the commander of the municipal staff of the Territorial Defence of Zenica. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Commander Saric also made it quite clear that the Mujahedin were not under the control of the army. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that this is a milinfosum and information that this witness gained possession of personally and confirmed it in answer to my questions, I move that this infosum be admitted into evidence as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, no objection.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, for the benefit of the transcript, the Defence is tendering the document, but also because of the truthfulness of paragraphs 3 and 4 contained in this milinfosum.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, will you give us a number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Exhibit number will be DH108.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kiggell, is it true, and I am interpreting your statement given to the Prosecutor, if I say that on the 14th of June you were present at a meeting between Lieutenant Colonel Duncan and Commander General Hadzihasanovic?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown Document DH72(ID) for me to be able to ask the witness some questions about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Will you please focus your attention on paragraph 1, please. As you explained yesterday, when attending these meetings, you kept notes, you kept a record of the meeting. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You will remember that at that meeting, the question of the Mujahedin was raised, and that the deputy commander Dzamal Merdan stated clearly on that occasion that the Mujahedin were not under the control of the 3rd Corps. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That was, in fact, stated at the end of this paragraph, the one-but-last sentence of paragraph 1 of this milinfosum. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Commander Hadzihasanovic told Lieutenant Colonel Duncan about his letter which he had addressed to the supreme command headquarters and showed it to him in order to convince him of the measures being taken by the 3rd Corps for the Mujahedin to be placed under control or removed from the area. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness now be shown a document dated the 13th of June, DH73(ID). A letter by Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Enver Hadzihasanovic dated the 13th of June.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The witness has the exhibit DH73(E-ID).

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember, Mr. Kiggell, that this is the letter shown to Lieutenant Colonel Duncan by Commander Hadzihasanovic during that meeting on the 14th of June?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot accurately recall if this was the letter.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you do know that the letter has to do with the Mujahedin and that it was addressed to the supreme command, and that it was shown to Lieutenant Colonel Duncan. This is stated in your milinfosum as well.

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's stated that a letter was shown, and obviously this is the one that relates to it because it's dated at the time and to the staff commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, in view of the fact that the witness was present at the meeting referred to in paragraph 1 of the milinfosum dated the 14th of June, I should like this document to be finally admitted into evidence and given an exhibit number. Also, the witness confirmed that on that day, a letter addressed to the supreme command was shown to Lieutenant Colonel Duncan, and that is why I would like this document to be admitted into evidence as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before giving the floor to Mr. Withopf, the Chamber wishes to recall that these two documents were given an ID number, DH72 and DH73, the reasons being that these documents had a direct link to Lieutenant Colonel Duncan, whose testimony has been planned. And that is why we gave a provisional number to these documents. The witness is familiar with the contents of paragraph 1 of the document dated the 14th of June. He is of the opinion that the letter should correspond to the letter mentioned in that document, but he is not telling us that he himself read that letter. Now, what are the comments of Mr. Withopf concerning the final admission of these two documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, in view of what the witness said, there's no objection by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. In view of the fact that the Prosecution has no objection, the numbers 72 and 73 now become final exhibit numbers. So Mr. Registrar, please confirm that these two documents have finally been given Exhibit Numbers 72 and 73.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I can confirm that now the documents are marked as admitted, DH72, DH73, and DH73(E).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Continue, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kiggell, as a liaison officer who was in the 3rd Corps Command on a daily basis, you certainly knew that the supreme command staff after this started to take measures against the Mujahedin asking them that they be either placed under control or that they leave the region. Were you familiar with those steps taken?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall those steps.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday, my learned friend from the Prosecution showed you the milinfosum dated the 20th of May 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So could the witness be shown Exhibit Number P99, please, dated the 29th of May 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 3 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your question, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, look again at paragraph 3, which you commented on yesterday. On the basis of the grid reference indicated in paragraph 3(a) , you marked the position of Fazlici. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I should like to ask you to look at a map which we will show you now. And it is Defence Exhibit DH98. It's a map in the scale of 1:25.000.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please place it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please point on the map to Fazlici, where allegedly the Mujahedin were seen.

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that north of Fazlici, several kilometres to the north, the last inhabited place towards the front line with the Serbs was Gluha Bukovica?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, if I were to tell you that that locality was still under the control of the army deep within the rear, would you agree with me then that Fazlici was not close to the front line? Because you can see where Gluha Bukovica is located.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Withopf.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecution objects to this question. This is a theoretical question. It's phrased "if I would tell you..." My learned friend obviously tries to somehow testify, and she makes or tries to make the witness comment on a theoretical situation. Nobody knows whether this situation is actually the correct situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, such questions are permissible, especially as I wish to refer to the comment in this milinfosum. And the Prosecution yesterday asked the witness several times to comment on the comments in the milinfosum. The places on the map have not been changed. The witness is a soldier, and he's able to answer that question. If the witness has been able to find the village of Gluha Bukovica, which is deep behind the front line, my question is: Is it true that in that case Fazlici is not close to the front line, the front line with the Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It would be better to ask him first to pinpoint the front line. Why don't you ask him whether he knows where the front line is, and then you can go on to your second question. So Witness, you have a map front of you. As you moved around in the area, could you point during -- using the parameters of the map where the front line was. And show us the front line with the pointer, if you remember. If you don't, tell us. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't accurately recall where the front line was. But the Serb front line was to the west, and then obviously there was the front line, area of conflict, with the Croats in this region. But I couldn't give you an accurate picture of where the front line is now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, we were not able to see what the witness marked on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Will you do that again, please. Point with the pointer to the front line with the Serbs approximately, if you remember.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't accurately remember. I just remember the front line being to the west on this map. I couldn't draw it on it. And the same with the line of confrontation with the HVO forces, I couldn't accurately do it. I just know the rough area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I'm addressing the Defence counsel. The witness is telling us that he cannot say where the front line was. Regarding the front line with the Serbs, he remembers that it was to the west, but he cannot provide any additional information. So please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kiggell, if you were to remind you and tell you that the front line with the Serb forces was on Mount Vlasic, would you then be able to express an opinion?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, my learned friend from the Defence continues with this line of questioning "if I would tell you..." My learned colleague is only allowed to ask questions that are based on the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. testimony of the witness. The witness is not here as an expert. And what my learned friend does, she actually testifies.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll withdraw the question to avoid further debate about it. But I would in that case --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Chamber thanks you for that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the map be removed, please, and could the witness be shown Prosecution map P98 on which the front lines have been marked. And I won't ask him about the front lines. But I will put a completely different question to him. So this map, could it be removed, and could the witness be shown the map that he looked at yesterday. It is Prosecution Exhibit P98.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He has the map in front of him now.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kiggell, yesterday you marked on this map the village Fazlici on the basis of the grid reference in the milinfosum. In the top corner, you have the front lines mark in the northwest. Can it be said, Mr. Kiggell, that Fazlici was significantly removed from the front line?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecution very strongly, very strongly objects to this question. Number one, this map doesn't have a date on it, and nobody is in a position to say as to when the markings were made and what situation, to what point in time such markings show. The Prosecution showed this map to the witness and tendered it into evidence for the only purpose to show a geographical location. It's an interpretation by the Defence that any of the markings do show a front line. The Prosecution objects.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'm surprised that the Prosecution would not provide a map that refers to the time period covered by the indictment. But let me just ask the witness that according to the best of his knowledge, do the lines indicate the front lines in 1993?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, I again object against this line of questioning, and the Prosecution would appreciate if the Chamber could rule on this issue. And of course, the Prosecution -- if Defence would be allowed to continue such questions, what lines is my learned friend making reference to? There are many lines on this map. And in respect to the comment of my learned friend that the Prosecution would not show a map that represents the situation in 1993, it's the view of the Prosecution that the geographical locations of villages like Fazlici were located in the very same area in 1993 and at any other time, before or after 1993. However, the Prosecution would appreciate if the Chamber could rule on this issue to avoid further discussion.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, perhaps the witness himself can tell us whether he can identify the front lines of the Serbs on this map. Maybe that is the only way for me to move on or to withdraw the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The Chamber notes that this document was produced yesterday by the Prosecution, and it was shown to the witness who at the time was a military officer with the rank of captain. This witness was a liaison officer, and within the framework of his mission he moved around in the area. He also explained that he was coming from Vitez to this area. He formally identified this village yesterday, thanks to the coordinates provided on the map. Of course, he couldn't be exposed to fire, but one could ask him whether, to the best of his knowledge, whether on this map which was a map used by the military: Witness, on the basis of this map, were there the positions of the hostile forces indicated often this map? Could you tell us? To the best of your recollection, because this was more than ten years ago, and the Chamber fully understands that it is difficult for you to recollect today certain facts of a very precise nature. However, looking at this map used by the military, could you tell us whether there were enemy forces there; if so, which; and where, roughly, were they positioned? And then, on that basis, perhaps we can move on to the question of the front line.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We had the Serbs to the west with the front line there with the 3 Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Sir, could you use the pointer to show the west on the map and the area that was under the control of the Serbs. Could you use the pointer to point to the positions of the Serbs. If you can remember them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't give accurate positions of the Serbs. I remember it being west of Travnik. And the Mount Vlasic was, I think, along the line of confrontation with the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you see Mount Vlasic on the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't think I can. I don't think that's Mount Vlasic. I think it's further west.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So the Serbs were to the west. As for the other forces, the Croats, where were they? Where was the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were centrally located around Vitez. And I'll just point to the map where I can roughly recall where they were situated. [Indicates] Very approximately.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Kiggell. Mr. President, may I continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kiggell, could you now have a look at the comment in the milinfosum, after item 3 that we have referred to, and where you have referred to Fazlici. The comment states that "it is quite apparent that large numbers of BH troops are still deployed along the confrontation line." On the basis of the map that you have, can you now confirm that Fazlici isn't the front line with the Serbian forces or in the vicinity of the front line where the Croatian forces are located? In fact, it is in between those two areas. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't accurately say which front -- it's more likely to be the HVO front line than the Serb front line.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. You pointed to Vitez. And at the time, there was fighting with the Bosniak forces there. Is that correct? However, Fazlici is not at the front line. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is just for the sake of the transcript. My learned friend asked a question "is that correct" and the witness wasn't given a chance to respond to this question. It's for the sake of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kiggell, I apologise if I didn't wait for your answer. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, I couldn't accurately recall that being the front line.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We can return this milinfosum. And I have further questions for the witness now. Yesterday, you also said that as requested by a Norwegian NGO you went to Arnauti. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The information you obtained when you visited Arnauti was mentioned in the milinfosum dated the 5th of June shown to you by the Prosecution yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown Prosecution Exhibit P100, please. Could the witness also be shown a map, the scale of which is 1:25.000, registered as Defence Exhibit 106.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kiggell, can you point to Arnauti on this map.

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kiggell, could you please show us where Zenica is located on the map. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's located to the west of this location. It's not physically shown on the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you confirm that Arnauti is in a removed part, removed area east of Zenica, and it is not that easy to reach Arnauti.

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. According to what is stated in the milinfosum under item 10B, you said that on that day, you confirmed that there was a training camp for the Mujahedin in Arnauti. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On that day, you did not see the persons who were being trained in that camp. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think according to the milinfosum I may have met them that day, and that's why I said "they have confirmed they run a training camp."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In fact, you met the Mujahedin. And it's the Mujahedin who confirmed that fact. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you did not meet the persons who may have been involved in training. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure exactly. I mean, I had a series of meetings. And whether on that day I met them or it was another occasion, I can't accurately recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, you have no information as to who went to the camp or as to who sent men to be trained in that camp. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. I mean, all we were aware of that the Mujahedin had set up the training camp, maybe to train fellow Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kiggell, would it be correct to say that at the time as the liaison officer you were aware of the fact that the army had an officers' school of its own for the education and training of its commanders. Were you familiar with that fact?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not for the BiH. I'm sure for the JNA army, as it was they had an officers' training school. But not the BiH. I wasn't aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But during the war in 1993, were you aware of the fact that an officers' school was established in Zenica, a school to train leaders in order to establish and develop the BH army? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please have a look at item 1. I apologise. Have a look at item 5, the heading of which is "Zenica." Have a look at item 5 in the milinfosum. And we can remove the map now. Yesterday, you commented on the facts mentioned under this item. They were mentioned by your battalion commander. Your attention was drawn to a sentence which says that it was possible to conclude that Bosnia and Herzegovina - I'm now paraphrasing this; it's the last sentence. It says that Bosnia and Herzegovina were not going to restrain themselves and were not likely not to take military initiative. This sentence was referred to yesterday. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That was on the 5th of June 1993. As someone in the 3rd Corps, you were aware of the fact that on the 4th of June 1993, the HVO from positions around Travnik attacked the town of Travnik. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would seem to be stated in the milinfosum.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were also aware of the fact that Velika Bukovica was attacked, and there were a significant number of victims who were observed there. Is that something you're familiar with?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I can recall. I'd obviously have to look at the milinfosum to give a description of what happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That fact is mentioned under item 3. It says: Alagic, Merdan and Kulenovic represented the BiH and Leutar the HVO. Merdan claims that 18 Muslims have been massacred in the village of Bukovica, and that something similar happened in Radojcici. That's the information contained in this milinfosum. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As a soldier aware of the difficult situation that the BH army was in, they were between two enemy lines, it was quite normal that the commander who had been attacked on the previous two days, it was quite normal that he would launch a counterattack in order to liberate, open up the passage between Travnik and Zenica. Was this something that was quite logical from a military point of view in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You were aware of the fact that after these attacks against Travnik and Velika Bukovica and other areas in the Bila valley, and the army continued with its counterattack and launched military activities throughout the area of the Bila valley. Were you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As a result, from the 6th to the 9th of June 1993, you were not able to have meetings with anyone from the 3rd Corps command, is that right, giving that fighting was ongoing at the time?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, the Prosecution also showed you a milinfosum dated the 23rd of June 1993. This is Prosecution Exhibit 501 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could it please be shown to the witness in order for me to ask the witness a number of questions. It's P101.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the transcript, it says 501. It should be corrected. It's 101.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, have a look at item 7. But before I ask you something about this item, I have some other questions I would first like to put to you. Mr. Kiggell, would it be correct to say that you personally never saw Mujahedin participating in combat operations together with the BH army?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't physically see them doing assaults, but I may have come across them at a checkpoint which I travelled through.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Similarly, to the best of your recollection, you can't remember anyone -- any of your colleagues saying at your meetings that they saw how the Mujahedin were present at the front lines when combat operations were being conducted. No one personally said that they had observed such a thing.

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it may have been mentioned, but I can't recall the incidents. The comment was that they were used as the elite troops in the front line.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But all you can remember is the comment made by your colleagues. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In June in Zenica, and in particular, from the 14th onwards -- from the 14th when you were at a meeting with General Hadzihasanovic and Lieutenant Colonel Duncan, and right up until the 23rd of June, you didn't see a single attack launched by the Mujahedin in Zenica itself? You did not observe a military attack carried out by the Mujahedin in Zenica. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I didn't observe any Mujahedin attack in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You can confirm, then, that the comment in the milinfosum under item 7, according to which the campaign in the Bila valley, we're referring to the combats of the 6th to the 9th of June, you have testified about this, these combats and the events in Zenica couldn't lead to the conclusion presented in this item. And this was shown to you yesterday. You cannot conclude that these events show that the Mujahedin were under the control of the 3rd Corps. Is that correct? The information that you had, the fact that you didn't see a Mujahedin attack of any kind in Zenica, and the fact that you didn't have any direct information about that participation in Bila, all this is contrary to the conclusion that --

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, I note that the question of my learned friend is about 10 or 11 lines long. And I also note that there Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. are -- is reference made to "these events." The Prosecution doesn't understand what events my learned friend is making reference to, other than the fact that the witness hasn't seen a Mujahedin combat operation in Zenica. So if my learned colleague could please ask a clear question to my -- to the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, ask the witness a precise question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kiggell, the comment says that the recent campaign in the Bila valley clearly shows that this is the case. "That this is the case" means control of the 3rd Corps over the Mujahedin. So my question is: On the basis of your personal experience, on the basis of what you saw in Zenica, and on the basis of what you saw in the village of Bila, on the basis of what you heard about, is it true to say that given all these factors one can't draw the conclusion that has been drawn here?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Withopf.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, the witness has been asked yesterday during the examination-in-chief a question of the very, very similar nature. He was asked by the Prosecution whether based on what he has seen, what he got to know attending the daily 1800 hours meetings and what he got to know from having talked to a variety of people he detailed yesterday, he can confirm this conclusion made under paragraph 8 of the milinfosum in front of the witness. The Prosecution is of the view that the witness has already answered this question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. He answered the question yesterday. Is the purpose of your question to get the witness to state the contrary today?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the purpose of the question is to have the witness tell us what he is aware of. Here, it says that they were participants in the campaign in the Bila valley. The witness answered my question and said that he never saw anything of this kind. He said that he only heard comments. Here, it says that this conclusion was drawn on the basis of the attack in Zenica. The witness said that there weren't attacks of any kind in Zenica. Given the facts that the witness is familiar with, my question for the witness is: Now that he has gone back to the events that he was a witness of, would he agree that this conclusion can't be reached on the basis of the facts that he is familiar with?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The problem concerns the way the question is presented. So you're asking this question to arrive at what the witness says, and then you tell the witness yesterday, in line X and Y, you said such and such a thing. Do you stand by what you said -- do you stand by what you say, or are you changing this statement? In such a case, there would be no problem, and the Prosecution couldn't object. I will now ask you the question. This is important. Yesterday, in response to a question put to you by the Prosecution, you said that, as it says in item 8, the Mujahedin were subordinated to the 3rd Corps. The Defence has asked you a series of questions, and you said that you couldn't confirm certain facts because you weren't present, or you said that there was hearsay evidence. You said that you didn't have such a precise vision, as it might -- or your vision wasn't as precise as it might have appeared initially. Today, it's Thursday, 10.30, do you now stand by what you said with regard to the Mujahedin, bearing in mind all the factors? This is what the Defence is pointing now to. You were a liaison officer in contact with the various individuals. Were they subordinated at the time to the 3rd Corps? Do you say that that is a hundred per cent concern? Or what can you tell us about this matter. Yesterday, you confirmed what was stated in item 8. What can you tell us about this today in light of the questions that have been put to you and that might have refreshed your memory? If you can answer the question, you'll answer it. If not, just tell us that you don't know the answer. What can you tell us about it? It's not a complicated matter.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Due to the information I had at the time, it was my opinion that the Mujahedin were used in attacks as they were perhaps the elite troops. They were more courageous. So my answer from yesterday in my opinion still stands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The Defence has heard the answer, which appears in line 15, page 33.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Continue, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the course of the meeting held on the 14th with Lieutenant Colonel Duncan and Commander Hadzihasanovic, as you've already said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's 10.30. It would be best to have a break now so that the interpreters can rest, unless Mr. Withopf has something to say. Mr. Withopf, what did you want to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I would only like to respectfully ask my learned friend from the Defence side how long she intends to continue with this series of questions? It's the view of the Prosecution that a significant number of the questions put to the witness today are irrelevant or even highly irrelevant. And I only wish to know as to how long this line of questioning is likely to continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Without making any judgement about the relevance or no relevance, how much more time do you need, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Another 15 minutes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 15 minutes. Mr. Dixon?

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we only have a few questions. We'll be no more than approximately 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Therefore, the Defence is telling us 30 minutes in all. The Judges will also have some questions. But as the Judges synchronise their questions, it won't take 30 minutes. And then of course you also will have the floor for re-examination. We will have the break, and we will resume at 5 to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The hearing is resumed. I give the floor to Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kiggell, you already said earlier on that at the meeting of the 14th of June, Commander Hadzihasanovic showed a letter to Lieutenant Colonel Duncan, and the letter has been admitted into evidence. Is it true that Lieutenant Colonel Duncan on that occasion did not comment on or challenge the letter shown to him by Commander Hadzihasanovic?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall whether he challenged the letter or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As far as the military situation in the 3rd Corps is concerned at the time that you were there, could you please answer a few questions for me. Is it true that at the time, the 3rd Corps had a confrontation line of several hundred kilometres against the Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that at the time there was a fierce conflict with the HVO forces?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that the HVO used as a powerful weapon against the BH army blockades of the main routes which also blocked the arrival of any kind of aid to Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that did occur.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that in the area of responsibility of the 3rd Corps in 1992 and 1993, more than a hundred thousand refugees had arrived from Eastern Bosnia, Krajina, Northern Bosnia, as well as from areas under the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. control of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was aware that a lot of refugees came into the area. Exact numbers I didn't know at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that in 1993, both the population and the military were confronted with extreme shortages of food, medicines, and other supplies, and that they depended heavily on humanitarian aid?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that there was constant fighting in Gornji Vakuf against HVO forces?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was a lot of fighting in that region.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true to say that the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina did not have sufficient equipment, nor resources to engage in such extensive combat operations?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true to say that at the end of June, a new front was opened to the north of Zenica in Zepce, and in the fighting there the HVO captured more than two-and-a-half thousand civilians?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew there was fighting in that region. Whether they caught two-and-a-half thousand civilians, I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you aware that at the time the HVO overtly cooperated with the Serb forces and let them take over a part of the territory that they had had control of?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that may have happened. But again, I can't accurately recall that fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As a military man with experience and in view of all these and other facts that I have not mentioned now, can you confirm that the corps commander waging two wars and at the same time the army was in the process of formation, that his position was untenable?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President. Mr. President, it may be a translation issue only, but it sounds a bit odd if my learned friend asks the witness "in view of all these and other facts that I have not mentioned now," how can the witness comment on facts that were not introduced?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you are quite right. The question could be put, but it should be limited to the facts that he is aware of, because if we say "other facts," but rather the facts the witness is aware of. Because you're asking the witness for an opinion, him being someone who in touch with the commander of the 3rd Corps. And you're asking him his opinion. But he can only testify on the basis of facts that he was aware of. And the Prosecution is quite right in making this point.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise to my learned friends, Their Honours, and the witness. I shall rephrase my question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: All these facts that I have now mentioned, and everything else that you personally were able to see during your stay in Zenica and in the area of the 3rd Corps, as a professional soldier, can you agree with me that the commander of the 3rd Corps in 1993 found himself in a virtually impossible situation?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At that stage of the confrontation, the BiH forces had suffered heavily, and they were now trying to regather themselves to try and fight their enemy. So it was a very hard time for BiH.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Very briefly, a few more questions for you. In answer to the President of the Trial Chamber, you expressed your opinion in connection with the comment that I showed you. My question now is, for things to be quite clear to me, is it true that in those days, there was quite a bit of confusion regarding the position of the Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And hence the comment in the milinfosum that with information we had at the time, we thought this they were working for 3 Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: To make things quite clear, could you please answer as briefly as possible, some question that I asked you already, but are the result of your own knowledge. Is it true that you met the Mujahedin for the first time at this coffee bar unarmed? Was that your answer?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think they were unarmed in the coffee bar.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The second time you met these three Turks who told you that they were not under the control of the army. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as I think reported in the milinfosum.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the 31st of May, you presented your own view that they were not under the army's control. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall. I think -- was that the result of my conversation with Merdan?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. We showed you that milinfosum, and it is an exhibit now. Commander Saric told you that they were not under their control. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the meeting on the 14th of June, deputy Merdan told you clearly that they were not under the army's control. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the same meeting with General Hadzihasanovic. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the time the letter was shown, the letter that I showed you here. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You did not see the Mujahedin involved in any combat operation?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not physically see them carry out an attack. As I said, I only saw them at checkpoints.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You saw them in Arnauti, at the training camp?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You knew that they were good fighters, and it was on that basis that you concluded that they might have been under the control of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a lot of information to say that the Mujahedin were there to help the 3 Corps efforts in fighting the war. So with all the other information that my colleagues had been collecting, that was our opinion at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: All the other information you were unable to convey to Their Honours because they were comments made by other persons. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the milinfosum, the intelligence officer would sort of analyse the information he'd received. So therefore, he's the one who wrote those comments on there. So therefore, he may have gathered that comment from the debriefing of the people on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, this opinion of yours, you were not able to corroborate personally with facts that you personally saw?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think it was comments made at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kiggell.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Madam. I turn now to the other Defence counsel who have some questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: May it please Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Kiggell. I have a few questions for you on behalf of Mr. Kubura. You said in your testimony yesterday, Mr. Kiggell, that you saw Mr. Kubura on occasions, and that you saw him at the headquarters of the 3rd Corps. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: You never actually had a formal meeting with him or any discussions with him?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only when I met him at 3 Corps. But I never met him at his headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: You met at 3 Corps only in passing by. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: He invited you on one occasion, did he not, to attend at his headquarters, the 7th Brigade headquarters?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: As you've said, that meeting never materialised for whatever reason, as you explained yesterday. So in the end, you never actually attended at the 7th Brigade headquarters for a meeting with him?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: You never met anybody else there in the headquarters?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: You were not functioning on the front lines. Your area of responsibility was Zenica and some of the surrounding parts?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. For a short stage only, I covered in the Vitez area. But naturally we sort of got to know the area, because of various problems we helped each other out, the liaison officers, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: You never travelled to the front lines to make observations?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in Zenica area, because we used the main routes, going over the mountain and through the bypass. So that was my sort of visual inspection when I crossed the front line at that stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: You never ever personally observed the 7th Brigade on the front lines in the field?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I think the only time I saw them was at the checkpoints.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that your direct knowledge of the 7th Brigade was, therefore, relatively limited, the structure of the brigade, the composition of that brigade?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: You said in your testimony yesterday that at the end of May, you reported that Mr. Kubura was the commander of the 7th Brigade, that that's recorded in a military information summary as well?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: That was the first time you knew that he was the commander?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: And that's how you understood his position, as "the commander"?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Did you know that he was a substitute commander or acting commander?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: The information that you used to find out this fact was the sources that you've mentioned time and time again, the people you spoke to on the ground?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: What other people told you?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was introduced to Mr. Kubura as the 7th Brigade commander I think when I was at the 3 Corps headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: In respect of the foreign fighters, the Mujahedin, you were not briefed about them and their presence in Central Bosnia before you arrived at the end of April?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall if we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: But when you arrived there, you didn't have detailed information about them?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: You have said in your testimony that you met them on three particular occasions. I don't wish to repeat all the details again. But I think it's important to pinpoint the dates. The first was in a cafe in the suburb of -- a suburb of Zenica. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: And there you saw some of these foreign fighters. They weren't armed. And that was at the end of May?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: So you had been there approximately a month already?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd actually been in the Zenica area for just over a week, I think it was. Because I came back down from Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Right. The second time was the camp in Arnauti.

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You know, it was...

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: That was on a date in early June?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: And there was another occasion which you mentioned meeting a number of foreign fighters, on the 31st of May or a date around then?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. Yes, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: When you met with them, they never mentioned the 7th Brigade to you?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think in one meeting, they wouldn't give me military information. I can't recall whether they then, in subsequent meetings they denied being part of 7 Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: But you can't recall whether they ever said anything to you about under whose control they were?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: In fact, in the military information summaries that we've seen in Court and in your reports, you don't mention that they are generally as you put it under the control of the 7th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: We have seen one report, which has been referred to on a few occasions, that being the one of the 31st of May. That's Prosecution Exhibit -- sorry, Defence Exhibit DH108. Where you formed the impression that they were not under the control of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Mr. Kiggell, can you confirm that in the middle of July, there were reports received that there was an assassination attempt on Mr. Kubura by foreign fighters, a group of Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there had been a report.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: You noted that in your diary, which you had. You had a war diary, did you not?

utterances.speaker: CAMERON KIGGELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: And the date of that was the 14th of July?
