utterances.text: One last issue, Major, I wish to discuss with you: Based on your experience and from what you experienced whilst you stayed in Central Bosnia between April 1993 and November 1993, how would you describe the communication abilities within the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: MARK WILLIAM BOWER
utterances.text: I got the impression that there was good communication in the fact that I knew by working in Stari Vitez, a Muslim enclave within the Croat pocket, the HVO-Croat pocket, that they had ready communications to 325 Brigade at the Cajdras checkpoint. And I also know that the Cajdras checkpoint had communication with 3 Corps because of my involvement with requests to go into Stari Vitez from, I think his name was Kulestra, 325 brigade. And he would say, he would have -- he knew that there were various casualties, whatever, because of his radio communications. And there were other occasions when he would stop me, or his troops would stop me from going through a checkpoint. He would say I he'd had orders, you know, I can speak to 3 Corps, they've told us. So whether it was by radio or by land line, I can't comment. But there certainly appeared to be communication ability between the various elements, down to the lowest level in the area where I operated in frequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Does this, Major, does it apply for the whole period of time you stayed in Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: MARK WILLIAM BOWER
utterances.text: From what I could recall, there would be days when communication would be not possible, and no other reason was given than that. But I would say generally, throughout the period of time, I would say the ability was there, but there could be times when communication was not possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Major. Mr. President, Your Honours, the Prosecution for the time being has no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. If I have understood you correctly, you have now concluded your examination-in-chief. We have another 15 minutes before the break. I'll make good use of these 15 minutes and let the Defence take the floor immediately.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would kindly ask you to tell us whether we will be working today as usual, in view of the fact that it is quite clear that both our team and our colleagues in the other team can finish the cross-examination quite quickly tomorrow so that maybe we don't have to work this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecution asked us to sit this afternoon. The Registry has taken steps to ensure a team of interpreters to be here as of 2.45. Therefore, we will be working from 2.45 until 4.15, and then tomorrow we'll begin at 9.00, and we'll be working nonstop until a quarter to 2.00. However, if you feel that you don't need so much time and that tomorrow's sitting will be quite enough, there are others, too. We have to see whether the Prosecution agrees. In that case, we don't have to sit in the afternoon. But you know best. If you are telling us that you only need one hour tomorrow, and also the other team one hour or less, and the Prosecution a quarter of an hour or no time at all, there's no problem. We wish to avoid the witness having to stay over the weekend. So what are you telling us?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I never intended to ask for more than two hours for the cross-examination of this witness, as the Prosecutor told us yesterday. However, as the Prosecutor abbreviated that period of time, I, too, will shorten my cross-examination. So that I don't believe it can take more than an hour and a half. If my colleagues don't have too many questions either, then it is quite certain that we can finish the cross-examination of this witness by midday tomorrow. And then the witness can leave without us having to work this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you said tomorrow, you'll be cross-examining from 9.00 to 10.30. Then there will be the break. We begin at 5 minutes to 11.00. Let me ask the other Defence team now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. We certainly won't be longer than half an hour tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Then 11.00 to 11.30. And let's hear Mr. Withopf now, because we have to measure our time. Can you tell us whether you will have possible re-examination tomorrow? Of course, that depends.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: That's exactly the point. It depends on the scope of the cross-examination and of course on the questions asked during cross-examination. However, it appears to be possible to conclude the testimony of this witness, if we don't continue today and would sit during the regular hours tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. In that case, obviously the best thing to do is to fit everything in tomorrow. So we don't need to continue this afternoon. And this will allow the Defence to contact their clients. And I think that we will finish tomorrow as envisaged. Therefore, you prefer to start your questions tomorrow? Is that right? Very well. In any case, we have only eight minutes left until the adjournment. So I'm grateful. Witness, you will come back tomorrow at 9.00. Because originally we had planned to continue this afternoon, but in view of the timing, your hearing will be resumed tomorrow morning. And rest assured, that it will be completed by a quarter to 2.00. I'm going to ask Madam usher to be kind enough to escort you out of the courtroom, inviting you to be back here tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the part of the Defence, are there any observations or remarks?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President, as we have a few minutes before the normal adjournment, I'd simply like at this stage to speak about Exhibit DH1, which is a videotape used at the very beginning of the trial. And as we have a few minutes at our disposal, it's simply to tell you that when that exhibit was tendered, after a lot of discussion between the technical department and the Defence, the complete videotape is much longer than the 45 seconds that were viewed on the first day of trial. In this connection, Mr. President, we were now able to isolate the exact scene that was viewed during the first day of hearing. A copy of the tape has been given to our friends on the Prosecution side. And now, the exhibit consists of only the scene viewed on the first day of trial. Therefore, I would simply like to ask the Chamber to be kind enough to substitute the new exhibit for the old one. And this is simply to say that DH1 shows only what was viewed on the first day of trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Withopf or Mr. Mundis, your opinion about this substitution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, in fact, Mr. Bourgon has provided us a copy. I have reviewed that tape, as it was a witness that I led in direct examination. And of course, the Prosecution has no objection to the substitution as proposed by my friend, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Very well. In that case, the Chamber, after consultations, orders that the videotape that was tendered at the time and given the Exhibit Number DH1, that the Registry replaces that tape with the new tape that has now been checked and reviewed by the Prosecution. So we have a copy of that tape, do we? So this is the new tape, which will be DH1. Mr. Withopf.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Since there are still five minutes left, I only wish to use this opportunity to inform the Trial Chamber that today we disclosed the B/C/S translation of the amended expert report of General Reinhardt to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The Defence now has in B/C/S the amended report of General Reinhardt. As the General has been planned for the months of May, the Defence will have plenty of time to study the document. Are there any other points to be raised? Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We also have an additional document that was disclosed without being fully translated from B/C/S into English. This was a document used during the testimony of -- but I need to go into private session to tell you that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, let us go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
